LanguageData.LizarbInterface.PointFilter.Tip: Samples the skin textures nearest-neighbour instead of smoothing them. Only looks right at a UI scale of 1x or 2x: at 1.25x a texel covers 1.25 screen pixels, so the outline comes out thick in places and thin in others.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Inset.Tip: Paints each element slightly inside its own area so neighbouring buttons no longer touch. Nothing in the layout moves, so labels and icons stay exactly where the game put them.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.TexturedBackground.Tip: Lays a tiling two-tone grunge over window and panel interiors instead of a flat colour. It repeats at its own size rather than stretching, so it looks the same in a small panel and a full-screen window.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.ShowAllFonts.Tip: Off by default. The short list holds only serif faces that stay readable at the sizes RimWorld draws at. Blackletter is left out on purpose: it is the most medieval thing on the machine and the least legible in a colonist list.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.TextOutline.Tip: Draws each label eight more times underneath the real one, offset by exactly one screen pixel in each direction, in a very dark shade of the current theme. Costs a little performance on text-heavy screens.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.OutlineTiny.Tip: Off by default. At around 10px the black ring closes the holes in a, e and g and the word turns into a smudge, most visible on the backstory titles in the character tab.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.WindowAnimation.Tip: A quick scale and fade. Skipped for the architect menu, the work tab and other main panels. Those are the game furniture, not dialogs, and they open constantly.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.ComponentsSection: Which surfaces this mod is allowed to reskin. Turn one off to hand it back to the game, or to another mod, without giving up the rest.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.SkinButtons.Tip: Every button, the main bottom bar, tooltips, float menu rows and the slider rail. They all share one draw call, so they share one switch.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.SkinWindows.Tip: The 9-sliced frame that replaces vanilla's flat box, and the background pattern that goes inside it.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.SkinTabs.Tip: Tabs are the one surface drawn by replacing the game's own method rather than swapping a texture, so this is the switch to try first against another UI mod.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.SkinWidgets.Tip: Checkboxes, radio buttons, the slider knob, command gizmos, the colonist bar plate and progress bar fills. Bars that carry their own colour (mood, health, research) are never touched: that colour is information, not style.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.SkinScrollbars.Tip: Drawn by Unity from shared styles rather than from a texture, so this one is applied by changing those styles. Turning it off puts them back immediately.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.Section: Colours each category button in the Architect menu by what the category is for. Categories from other mods get a stable colour of their own.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.ColorLabels.Ti: Off by default: against a coloured button, text in the same hue loses contrast. Turn it on if you set the button colour strength to zero.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.AutoColor.Tip: Categories added by other mods get a stable colour generated from their defName instead of staying grey.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.Icons: Use this mod own category icons
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.Icons.Tip: Draws a white glyph with a black outline on the left of every category button. Categories from other mods are matched on their name, so Storage gets a crate and Genetics gets a cross.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.Icons.Clash: Architect Icons is active and draws its own icon in the same place. Turn one of the two off.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.PlateStyle.Pla: Fills the button, following the theme corner radius, and deepens towards the bottom.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.PlateStyle.Fra: Colour around the rim, centre left clear.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.PlateStyle.Fla: A plain rectangle, ignoring the theme shape.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.GrainOnButtons.Tip: Tiles the same pattern across button, tooltip and menu faces, not just window backgrounds. With the Grimoire skin this is what gives the buttons their parchment.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.AutoWidth: Widen the menu to fit the labels
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.AutoWidth.Tip: Vanilla fixes the Architect menu at 200px, which fits the stock font and the English Core names and nothing else. This measures the longest category name in the font you actually chose and widens the menu until it fits. It never makes the menu narrower.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.PlateStyle.Tag: A label with a point on its right.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.PlateStyle.Shi: A shield, heavier at the top.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.PlateStyle.Gra: A solid square, fading out to its right.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.Architect.ShapeOutline.T: Rings the shape in black, which keeps it separate from the button underneath. Painted as the same shape one pixel larger behind, so it follows whatever shape is chosen.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.AnimateMainTabs.Tip: Architect, Work, Schedule and the rest of the bottom bar. These open constantly, so the animation is felt far more often here than on a dialog.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.AnimateImmediate.Tip: The inspect pane and the other panels the game rebuilds every frame. They come and go with what is selected, so this fires often.
LanguageData.LizarbInterface.AnimateOther.Tip: Any window on a layer the three above do not cover.
